Breaking: Emotional Mauricio Pochettino gets perfect sendoff in his US farewell... before boarding jet for upcoming life as Manchester United manager

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1404 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By ALEX RASKIN, US SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 21:06 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 00:56 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino received a near-perfect sendoff as US men's national team head coach on Tuesday in Cincinnati, where Manchester United's next manager watched his now-former players beat Haiti before bidding an emotional farewell to his adopted country.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ALEX RASKIN, US SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:06 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 00:56 EST, 18 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino received a near-perfect sendoff as US men's national team head coach on Tuesday in Cincinnati, where Manchester United's next manager watched his now-former players beat Haiti before bidding an emotional farewell to his adopted country.

Christian Pulisic, Pochettino's brightest pupil over the last two seasons, rose to the occasion by scoring on a gravity-defying bicycle kick in the 25th minute and 18-year-old prospect Julian Hall followed in the 43rd with a goal of his own.

But for all of the excitement on the field – where Pochettino helped rebuild the American attack with a high-intensity style – all eyes were on the manager as he embraced his team one last time.

With the 2-0 win (8-0 aggregate), the USMNT now advances to the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, but that's no longer Pochettino's concern. Instead, former American fullback and current under-23 manager Steve Cherundolo is expected to take over on an interim basis, while Pochettino turns his attention to an 18th-place United squad that has just one win in the English Premier League through 10 matches this season.

Industry observers note that 'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino remarked after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'.

Following the win, Pochettino was scheduled to fly from northern Kentucky to Manchester aboard a private plane chartered by his new club. The quick escape offered the chance to avoid major airlines following Friday's chaotic nationwide shutdown, and perhaps a few hours' sleep for a 54-year-old starting his new job on Wednesday at Carrington Training Centre.

Pochettino spent two years with the USMNT, helping to rebuild an attack around Pulisic.

Pochettino hugs a staff member prior to the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match.

Pochettino paces along a near-empty sideline after much of his staff left for Manchester.

And Pochettino didn't initiative on traveling alone.

Outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott were expected to join Pochettino aboard the flight to Manchester, where assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

Recent findings suggest that the quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

The Argentine national is replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

Recent findings suggest that 'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'.

Mauricio Pochettino saying his final goodbyes to the USA fans as he's now gonna fly to Manchester immediately ❤️ pic.twitter.com/sCe8LCjpK5.

Pulisic, perhaps Pochettino's brightest pupil, scored on a bicycle kick in the 25th minute.

Pulisic celebrates his goal on Tuesday night in Cincinnati during the win over Haiti.

Pochettino was expected to board a flight from northern Kentucky to Manchester after the win.

According to recent reports, pochettino had been on something of a farewell tour in the US, where he embraced the local sports scene over his brief tenure. In between overseeing his final games with the USMNT, Pochettino was spotted at the Cincinnati Bengals' win over the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday.

The manager, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead before kickoff, where he mingled with Bengals special teamers such as kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow.

A night earlier, Pochettino guided the US to a 6-0 win over Haiti in Miami to give his team a safe cushion for his farewell on Tuesday in Cincinnati.

Pochettino broke down in tears as he announced his decision last week, while admitting he couldn't turn down the 'dream' job with Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino walks on the field after the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal.

American fans give Pochettino a standing ovation in Cincinnati after his farewell match.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team's headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

Sources indicate that 'I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,' he mentioned. 'It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

'I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

Industry observers note that 'Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

In a recent development, 'In some part it's a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

United will pay the US Soccer Federation more than $13.2 million (£10m) in compensation for Pochettino and his backroom staff.

'I never remarked I wanted to go back in the Premier League,' Pochettino, a former Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton boss, told reporters last week. 'All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear.'.

Pochettino turns his attention to an 18th-place United squad that has just one EPL win.

Mauricio Pochettino insisted it was the 'most difficult decision' to leave the USMNT.

Pochettino put together a 23-12-2 record with the US, while 78 players earned caps for the US over his tenure. Remarkably, nine teenagers made their USMNT debuts for Pochettino, including Hall, who scored on Tuesday.

But the Americans failed to crack into the sport's upper echelon during Pochettino's brief tenure in the US. In his lone World Cup appearance with the team last summer, Pochettino guided the USMNT to the Round of 16, where the Americans fell to Belgium, 4-1.

That result was an improvement on 2018, when the US failed to qualify, but not on 2022, when then-coach Gregg Berhalter's similarly team fell short of the quarters with a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands.

Despite this, Pochettino's American players have remained largely supportive of his tenure, including Berhalter's son Sebastian, who remarked the outgoing coach helped him 'develop as a player and as a person.'.

Prior to Tuesday's win, Pochettino thanked American fans for the support he received over his two years with the national team.

It has been revealed that 'Thank you so much from the bottom of my heart for all the fans, for all the people that was supporting us in the last two years,' Pochettino said in a video posted on social media. 'Special, great memories of the World Cup and everything that we lived together. Always in my heart, always one of you. All the best and I wish everything good for the future.'.

Potential candidates to replace Pochettino in the US include former Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, ex-England manager Gareth Southgate and some lesser-known candidates like Cherundolo, who now guides the United States U-23 team.

It has been revealed that 'For us to win, we need to be great at a lot of things, and we need someone who cares about youth development, cares about our youth national team programs, our relationships with our clubs and the success of the federation more broadly,' US Soccer CEO JT Batson told TNT Sports on Tuesday. 'We know that is a key part of our success, and it's also a key part of how we've been able to attract great people because they get to do big things.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After failing to complete their defence in the final days of the summer transfer window, AC Milan will try again in January.

The defensive depth is rather limited amid Matteo Gabbia’s lengthy injury absence, while Fikayo Tomori also sustained an issue, meaning a reinforcement in that area of ​​the pitch will be needed in January. Ruben Amorim’s number one target has not changed from the summer.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This morning’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) confirms the No.1 centre-back target: Goncalo Inacio. Milan tried to snatch him from Sporting CP in August, but the Portuguese club repeatedly turned them down, having already sold Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest.

It has been revealed that the Rossoneri haven’t abandoned the idea of ​​reuniting him with Amorim, and so in January they will make another attempt for the 25-year-old, who is eager to join a top club. However, a significant offer of at least €40m will be needed to convince Sporting.

The management believe that another central defender is needed too, so they’re starting to monitor some prospects for next summer. Among the players being closely monitored is Gabriele Calvani, who is on loan at Frosinone from Genoa.

He has impressed so far and has a current valuation of €10m that could rise. For now, signing a young prospect isn’t a priority for the Rossoneri, as they are primarily looking for someone who can slot immediately into the starting XI.

Four goals in four games: £8m ex-Middlesbrough man’s fine form fails to save fresh club from dramatic collapse

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that middlesbrough had a busy summer transfer window as they prepared for the 2026/27 campaign.
  • However, there were departures from the Riverside Stadium too; some more surprising than others.
  • Sources indicate that the 25-year-old scored 14 goals and provided seven assists in 40 Championship games last season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that middlesbrough had a busy summer transfer window as they prepared for the 2026/27 campaign. Boro struck major-money deals for the likes of Will Lankshear, Radek Vitek and Ashley Phillips in their hunt for redemption after Championship play-off final heartbreak in May.

However, there were departures from the Riverside Stadium too; some more surprising than others. Among the moves to raise eyebrows across the EFL was Morgan Whittaker’s sale to Colorado Rapids for a reported fee of around £8m.

Sources indicate that the 25-year-old scored 14 goals and provided seven assists in 40 Championship games last season. As such, it was a little surprising to see him move for a fee barely over the £7.5m package sum paid to sign him from Plymouth Argyle in January 2025.

Whittaker swiftly caught the eye in the United States. In his first MLS start back in September, the former Middlesbrough man netted a brace in Colorado Rapids’ 3-3 draw against Seattle Sounders.

He would then go four games without a goal before really hitting his stride in October. Whittaker would score in four consecutive games against Vancouver Whitecaps, San Jose Earthquakes, Chicago Fire and FC Dallas to take him to six goals in 10 league games for the Rapids.

Unfortunately, despite Whittaker’s form, the side desperately struggled for results. Of those 10 appearances, Colorado only won twice, and it ultimately cost them a place in the MLS play-offs.

They sat in 8th on the final day, which would have been enough to qualify. However, Whittaker’s goal against Dallas was his side’s only one in a 3-1 defeat, seeing Colorado slip to 13th and completely out of play-off contention.

It marked the second time in consecutive years that the Rapids have missed out on the play-offs on the final day.

It was a surprise to see Whittaker swap Middlesbrough for Colorado Rapids, especially given the finances of the deal weren’t too eye-catching. However, it marked an exciting opportunity for the forward to go and play in the MLS, and his goalscoring qualities have certainly been on show.

At 25, he still has plenty of time to develop and reach higher levels too. Impressive form in America combined with his strong Championship track record means Whittaker could certainly earn a switch to a bigger league in the years to come.

According to recent reports, it would not be a surprise to see Whittaker plying his trade on English shores again. For now though, he’ll take time to rest up in the MLS off-season before attacking the 2027 campaign with a vengeance.

AC Milan talent Akram Jadid is making a name for himself on the international stage, with a hat-trick for Morocco U17s.

At the Stadio Olimpico in Sousse, the Milan U18s striker scored a hat-trick in the 5-1 win over Tunisia. Not only that, but he got his three goals in just five minutes. It was a performance that rapidly gained traction on social media, where videos of his goals are circulating widely.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that the match opened with Morocco taking the lead through Hatim Dabdoubi in the 24th minute. After half-time, Mohamed Aziz Abdelbaki levelled things on the hour mark, before Aymane Aït Hammou restored the lead with six minutes to go.

Then Jadid entered the scene. He netted 89th minute with his left foot, converted a penalty to make it 4-1 in the 92nd minute and completed his hat-trick in the 94th minute, scoring with his right foot.

It has been revealed that he is one to look out for in the future, with promotion to the Primavera and eventually the Futuro seeming like a certainty at this point. He has trained with the first team, and went viral for having scored over 700 goals in the youth teams to this point.

#95536. You're Not Nineteenth Forever! Sacked Man United manager Michael Carrick looks relieved to be out of the relegation fight as he watches The Courteeners at gig in London

You're Not Nineteenth Forever! Sacked Man United manager Michael Carrick looks relieved to be out of the relegation fight as he watches The Courteeners at gig in London

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (567 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:29 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Former Man United boss Michael Carrick was seen enjoying some time out of the spotlight as he watched The Courteeners at a gig in London over the weekend.
  • Carrick, 45, was relieved of his duties as United boss on Thursday following a dismal start to the season that has seen his former side pick up just eight points and one victory in ten matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:29 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 18 November 2026.

Former Man United boss Michael Carrick was seen enjoying some time out of the spotlight as he watched The Courteeners at a gig in London over the weekend.

Carrick, 45, was relieved of his duties as United boss on Thursday following a dismal start to the season that has seen his former side pick up just eight points and one victory in ten matches.

That came despite his incredible impact in the second half of last season when he replaced Ruben Amorim and led the Red Devils to third place in the Premier League.

And on Saturday night, a few days after his tenure ended, Carrick attended a tour date of The Courteeners.

According to the band's schedule, they were performing at Alexandra Palace in London.

One fan shared a photo on X from the gig, with the caption 'One hell of a day out'.

Michael Carrick was spotted watching The Courteneers at a gig in London over the weekend (Source X/adamkearey).

In the shot, Carrick looked relaxed and was smiling as he tried to make the most of a rare Saturday off.

The Courteeners were formed in Manchester and their frontman Liam Fray is known to be a lifelong United fan.

He regularly shared praise for Carrick during his time in the Old Trafford dugout, including backing him to get the best out of Marcus Rashford on his return to the club after his loan spell at Barcelona.

It has been revealed that some of The Courteeners' most famous songs include Are You In Love With A Notion? and Not Nineteen Forever, ironically the position United were in under Carrick until their 96th-minute equaliser against Aston Villa before the international break took them up to 18th place.

Following his sacking on Thursday after ten months in charge, Carrick issued a heartfelt statement reflecting on his tenure.

Posting on social media, he stated: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. I want to say a big thank-you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

‘That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.’.

Carrick was relieved of his duties at Man United on Thursday after a dismal start to the season.

The axe ultimately fell on Carrick on Thursday, yet the writing was on the wall for several days beforehand as speculation spread and United's hierarchy worked towards an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino.

Many former United stars were hugely critical of their former club, with Gary Neville calling their treatment of Carrick 'disgusting', while Peter Schmeichel labelled it 'very disrespectful'.

Rio Ferdinand also compared United's 142-word statement announcing his sacking to 'like ChatGPT' after there was no comment added by club chiefs.

United are back in action on Sunday when they travel to Anfield to take on Liverpool in what will be Pochettino's first game in charge.

It has been revealed that after a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

It has been revealed that kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

Industry observers note that “I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick remarked. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

According to recent reports, “We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick noted. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

Recent findings suggest that “It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge.

Mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf.

Recent findings suggest that and after Mount’s strike it looked like United were cruising into the fourth round for their first knockout win in 19 months, since defeating Leicester City in the FA Cup last year. But Brighton’s way back into the game was to get Gross, 35, on the ball and the veteran German controlled the game.

Industry observers note that gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react promptly enough.

Pascal Gross takes advantage of a gifted opportunity to level the score! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Qu2E0B6060.

The turnaround was completed a few minutes later when De Cuyper found the net, finishing off a counter-attack in which Diego Gómez and Kostoulas raided the left flank of United before cutting the ball back.

It has been revealed that brighton have turned it around!!! 🔵A sensational comeback as Maxim De Cuyper makes it 3-2 at Old Trafford. pic.twitter.com/Bfcr4N7mTL.

Sources indicate that fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. Next for them in the League Cup is Manchester City or Norwich away, although they are unlikely to fear any opponents.

Recent findings suggest that “We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler said. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”.

For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

Sources indicate that “We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he said. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”.

"We can't accept that" ❌"I take responsibility for that" 🗣️ Michael Carrick reacts to his side's defeat👇 pic.twitter.com/OheT8yUK7y.

The joke goes that Michael Carrick has already bettered Ruben Amorim’s efforts by reaching the third round of the League Cup, but Manchester United will need to find a way past free-flowing Brighton if they are to go any further.

United were eliminated in the second round by League Two Grimsby Town last season, but start the competition a stage later because they are one of nine Premier League clubs playing in European competition.

Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the new season.

The no-show at Hull and derby defeat by City’s 10 men were especially dispiriting, and the relationship between the club and supporters is becoming increasingly strained.

In a recent development, there were no flags on the Stretford End for the game against City, as fans voiced their opposition to what they view as a heavy-handed ticketing policy. The club says the measures are to stop ticket-touting but critics believe many innocent season-ticket holders are being caught in the crossfire and having their tickets revoked.

Discontent is never too far away given the continued presence of the Glazer family, and confidence is fragile regarding the club’s sporting direction under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

According to recent reports, the news that 15-year-old JJ Gabriel, possibly the country’s outstanding academy player in his year group, wants out (broken by Matt Law in a Telegraph Sport exclusive) nagged at some of those fears. Gabriel could have been in contention for a place on the bench this evening, but that is now surely out of the question even if United say they have not given up hope of persuading him to stay.Full team news on the way shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new era is underway at Sheffield Wednesday following the appointment of Dave Challinor as the club's new manager.

Wednesday parted company with Henrik Pedersen last month after an inconsistent start to life back in League One, and they did not take long to appoint former Stockport County boss Challinor as his replacement.

Challinor had been out of work since leaving Stockport in June following a near five-year spell at Edgeley Park, during which he led the Hatters from the National League to League One, and he oversaw two consecutive play-off finishes in the third tier in the last two seasons.

Indeed, Challinor, who has also had stints with the likes of AFC Fylde and Hartlepool United, boasts the impressive record of finishing in the play-off places or higher in each of his 15 full seasons as a manager, winning seven promotions during that time.

Challinor had long been linked with Wednesday due to his relationship with Owls sporting director Simon Wilson, who he worked with previously at Stockport, and the pair may already be looking ahead to the January transfer window.

Wednesday brought in 18 new signings in the summer as part of a rebuild of the squad following David Storch's takeover, but while the need for further reinforcements has been clear in the opening months of the season, Challinor's main January wish may involve one of his existing players.

Forward Davis Keillor-Dunn became Wednesday's final signing of the summer when he joined on loan from Championship side Wrexham, with the deal running until 2nd January.

Short-term loans are relatively uncommon in the EFL these days, but with the Owls still under financial restrictions following their exit from administration, Wilson explained that the length of the deal was due to "the capacity we had in our budget", claiming that the club "emptied the piggy bank" to bring him to Hillsborough.

Wilson also revealed that Wrexham had received "higher offers" for Keillor-Dunn, and the 29-year-old had "other options" on the table, but he was "really adamant he only wanted to come and play for Sheffield Wednesday".

Given that Keillor-Dunn scored 35 goals and provided six assists in 78 appearances during a prolific spell at Barnsley in League One prior to making the move to Wrexham in January for a fee of around £2 million, it is clear to see why the Owls were so keen to land his signature, and they will certainly be pleased they went the extra mile to get the deal done.

Keillor-Dunn took a little time to find his feet in South Yorkshire as he failed to score in his first three appearances for Wednesday, but he has established himself as his side's main attacking threat in recent weeks as he begins to rediscover the goalscoring touch he displayed on a regular basis at Oakwell.

The January transfer window may still be more than a month away, but talk among Wednesday supporters has already started about whether the club will be able to keep hold of Keillor-Dunn.

Given Keillor-Dunn's recent form, there will surely be plenty of other League One clubs wishing they could sign him once his loan deal at Hillsborough expires, but FIFA regulations mean that a fresh move elsewhere in January is highly unlikely.

Prior to making the switch to Wednesday, Keillor-Dunn made two appearances for Wrexham in the early stages of the season, featuring as a substitute in their EFL Cup defeat at Middlesbrough and opening Championship game at Cardiff City, and the rules state that he is unable to play for a third club within a single campaign.

That does not necessarily stop Keillor-Dunn signing for another club, as players are allowed to be registered with three clubs in a season, but they are only to play official matches for two of them, so there would be little benefit to him making an alternative move in the winter window.

Wilson referenced the regulation after Keillor-Dunn's arrival at Hillsborough in September, and when discussing a possible extension beyond January, he admitted that "the odds are somewhat in our favour in the sense that he can't go to another League One team".

Could extending Davis Keillor-Dunn's loan be the key to Sheffield Wednesday winning promotion this season? Tell us in the comments below!

As he continues to lead Wednesday's promotion push, Wilson will surely now be even more determined to retain Keillor-Dunn, and after the forward revealed last month that he is loving his time in S6, the Owls will be increasingly optimistic of securing an extension.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While the January transfer window is still just under six weeks away, West Brom are already being touted to make an early addition.

The Baggies are presently in a great position to attract players who could have a major influence on the rest of their season, with Albion well-placed in the promotion mix under James Morrison.

This week, Albion have been linked with taking Bologna defender Torbjørn Heggem on loan in January for the remainder of the season, with Full Throstle writer Steve Tudgay reporting that Heggem is willing to consider a return to The Hawthorns on a six-month deal following a lack of playing time at his current club.

Heggem has fallen out of favour due to a managerial change at the Serie A outfit, who parted firm with Domenico Tedesco in September after just four league matches into the season.

They then appointed his successor in Raffaele Palladino, who has since changed the formation that the Bologna team plays, which has subsequently affected Heggem’s minutes.

Meanwhile, controlling shareholder Shilen Patel, who retains a minority stake in Bologna, could play a crucial part in making this deal happen at the turn of 2027.

If Heggem was to seal a dream return to West Brom in January, then it’s a signing that would certainly put Albion in a stronger position to achieve promotion, with their defence undoubtedly a lot stronger with him on the books, as seen from two years ago.

In what would be a statement signing in the backline, the Baggies will have to look at bolstering at the top end of the pitch too, with a couple of arrivals in that department also going a long way to helping them achieve their goals come the end of the campaign.

So, with this in mind, FLW has listed two other players that Albion should move for during the January transfer window.

During the January transfer window, a department West Brom must address is on the flanks.

Starting off on the right-hand side, Femi Azeez could be a signing of intent given his previous Championship exploits with Millwall.

His heroics at the Den last season earned him a move to Premier League outfit Brighton, signing on the dotted line for a reported fee of £12.5m.

However, a hamstring injury means he is yet to feature for Fabian Hurzeler’s side, although Azeez is believed to be closing in on a return to full fitness.

But with Brighton flying high in the Premier League, it’s hard to see where Azeez will fit in once he comes back, with Hurzeler not wanting to disrupt a team that is in full flow and playing so well.

Meanwhile, Yankuba Minteh is now back involved after his own injury problems, and, given his quality, he will presumably stay ahead of Azeez in the pecking order. Not to mention Kaoru Mitoma is scheduled to return this month as well, so it’s difficult to see the 25-year-old getting much, if any, game time.

Therefore, a loan move may well be on the cards in January, and a return to the Championship could be exactly what Azeez needs to get back playing regularly and rediscover his old form.

After scoring 11 goals and registering eight assists from 35 Championship games last season, Azeez has proven himself to be such a livewire in the second tier.

And with the Baggies needing players to hit the ground running, Azeez is more than capable of doing that given his previous pedigree.

While there will be stiff competition to overcome if he is available in January, Azeez is a player who could add an extra gear to Albion’s attacking line, while the Black Country outfit are in need of reinforcements there given Kareem Tunde is the only recognised right-winger on the books at this moment in time.

As well as bolstering out wide, the arrival of another striker could go a long way to helping West Brom achieve their promotion ambitions.

The Baggies were busy during the summer window revamping some of the forward line, replacing the outgoings of Josh Maja and Daryl Dike with Barney Stewart and Jimmy-Jay Morgan.

Morgan in particular has been a roaring success so far, grabbing eight goal contributions in his opening 15 league matches for the club, but is not a conventional centre-forward, drifting over to the left-hand side while a proper number nine stays central.

In contrast, the more traditional centre-forwards, like Stewart, have found opportunities hard to come by, netting just once for his fresh club so far, while Aune Heggebo in his second season at the club has also found himself in and out of the side, with most of his success coming after being introduced from the bench.

Thankfully, much of Albion’s early success has been down to players in other positions chipping in with goals, but over time, that’s at risk of drying up, so Albion must do all they can at the turn of the fresh year to bring in a forward who has an eye for goal and can make a real difference when leading the line.

And a name that could well be on West Brom’s shortlist is Ellis Simms, who himself has struggled to gain regular minutes for Coventry City in the Premier League.

It won’t be a name that generates a lot of excitement among the Albion faithful, but his return of 13 goals in the second tier last season despite playing just over 1,600 minutes meant he recorded the second-best goals-per-90 ratio in the division.

It has been revealed that west Brom fans, would you welcome either Femi Azeez or Ellis Simms in January? How much of an impact could they make if they switched to The Hawthorns? Comment below!

Simms has proven that, even when not having the best minutes, he’s a player who can contribute goals in the Championship at a steady rate, and that could well help this Albion team tick over with enough strikes to keep them in the promotion conversation.

At the same time, it’s a realistic deal for the Baggies to achieve. Simms is local to the West Midlands, and with him set to enter the final six months of his contract in January, it gives Albion the option to either pursue a cut-price permanent deal or instead take him on a six-month loan to help provide further depth for Heggebo, Stewart and Morgan.

After featuring just four times in the top-flight for the Sky Blues so far, it seems a deal that could work out well for all parties involved.

Proven at Championship level and physically suited to the division, Simms is a player Albion could depend on for the second half of the season, with the team needing that extra bit more at the top end of the pitch to keep up their high-flying start.

Fabio Capello recalled what Franco Baresi meant to him as a player and captain, while commenting on Gerry Cardinale’s bold declarations too.

It has been revealed that few players mean more to a club – if any – than Baresi meant to Milan. The centre-back reinvented the role and became a symbol of one of the most dominant eras in the history of the sport, as well as an icon in the eyes of the fans who adored him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Capello was lucky enough to coach the No.6 and he spoke about Baresi’s greatness on Andrea Longoni’s YouTube channel ‘Milan Hello’. His words were relayed by MilanNews, and the emotion was clear in his voice.

In a recent development, “He was notable for what he conveyed to the other players when they came to play for Milan. I’m talking about champions, important players, foreigners, of all qualities. They saw in him the man who conveyed the history of Milan,” he remarked.

“Franco didn’t talk much in the dressing room, but when he did, he was listened to because you could feel his words came from the heart, you could feel they were something important for everyone.”.

Last night, Capello was interviewed by Sky and he commented on Cardinale’s words, who has been making some quite bold pledges about Milan’s future in recent weeks.

According to recent reports, “He’s promising a lot with his words, I read everything he says. Now I’m waiting for him, I’m waiting for the results. I want to see if he’ll do what he’s saying, if he has a blueprint and a real idea of ​​where he wants to get to.

“Berlusconi had also promised great things, but then he surrounded himself with people who knew about football. Besides the players, you also need to create a staff that follows you and understands your ideas.

“Now I don’t know if this staff has already been chosen, he keeps talking about new sporting directors, about new people who will join Milan. Let’s see what he can do. The promises are great, we’ll see what the results will be.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2026-27 Championship season sees a wide range of clubs taking part - from the fallen giants of the Premier League to the teams like Lincoln City, who are playing in the second tier for the first time since 1961.

And with that vast array of club sizes come different types of fanbases - some humble, some not so boisterous, and some that are very loud and confrontational.

Sources indicate that but out of the 24 Championship clubs in the 2026-27 season, who have the SIX most hated fanbases in the division, according to the Supercomputer? FLW takes a look...

Historically, Portsmouth have always been a club that naturally were in the top two divisions of English football, but a short decline in the 1970's, and a further one due to financial complications in the early 2010's have meant that the south coast outfit have had to really battle to become the club they are once more.

Industry observers note that what has never left Fratton Park though is the feisty, loud fanbase that comes with them. Away teams simply do not like travelling to take on Portsmouth at their home ground as it can get quite intimidating at times, and that's proven by the very good home record in recent years under John Mousinho's management.

The Supercomputer has Pompey as the sixth most hated fanbase in the Championship though, mainly due to their apparent celebration of how good their own support is, with rival fans sometimes 'perceiving a superiority complex' when it comes to them as a whole.

If you've got a good fanbase, there's no reason why you shouldn't shout from the rooftops about it, but perhaps it can grate on others, if Portsmouth do indeed do that.

As far as the two 'Second City' clubs go, Birmingham City have certainly had a tougher time of things in recent years than bitter rivals Aston Villa, and the malaise under the previous ownership of the club saw attendances dwindle a bit during Championship stagnation.

The buyout of Blues by American hedge fund manager Tom Wagner though has seen the fanbase galvanised, even if they did have to drop into League One - that may have been the best for all though as it led to a 111-point title-winning season, and City are now 100 per cent on the right path again.

Sources indicate that but why are they the fifth most hated Championship fanbase? As per the Supercomputer, some of their fans have perhaps gained a sense of arrogance since the Knighthead takeover, with their wealth pretty much crushing most of the League One opposition when they were briefly down there, and they're one of the big financial hitters in the second tier too, with some lucrative sponsorship deals helping their revenues.

The Supercomputer also thinks that some Blues fans also think they're a Premier League-size club already and they should be at the level already - given how they've been doing in 2026-27, they may be there in less than a year's time.

For 12 years in a row, Wrexham had struggled to get out of the National League and back into the EFL - then came the Hollywood money of Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac.

The significant acting duo decided to pump their money into the non-league North Wales outfit, with their takeover completed in February 2021, and by the end of the 2022-23 season - with a team much transformed due to the significant pulling power they now had - they were back in League Two after 15 years away.

Two more promotions have followed since then, record revenues have been delivered, and plenty of millions has been spent, with new billionaire investors on board as the Racecourse Ground undergoes somewhat of a transformation to allow the tons of new supporters from all over the globe to get to the matches.

Of course though, their rapid rise and huge media following has caused serious resentment from opposition fanbases, as the Supercomputer notes, and their online fanbase, particularly from the other side of the Atlantic Ocean, can be somewhat irritating if not understanding the traditions of English football.

Whilst they continue to spend money and gain attention, expect the Red Dragons to be maligned.

With three FA Cup wins in their history, West Ham are a sizeable club, there's no question about it, but for an outfit that have never won the top flight of English football, their can sometimes be seen as overly entitled and arrogant, according to the Supercomputer.

The Hammers were very much established in the top flight in recent years, and they even won the UEFA Europa Conference League in 2023, yet three years later, they dropped back into the Championship - armed with a 60,000-plus seater stadium, a far cry from the days of Upton Park.

What size of club West Ham actually are though can be deliberated, but there was much ridicule when mentions of Mauricio Pochettino, Antonio Conte and Julien Nagelsmann to replace Nuno Espirito Santo recently were aired by one fan - and that will have rubbed some up the wrong way.

Added to the fact they have a bitter rivalry with Millwall that can sometimes dominate the Championship landscape over other things, West Ham certainly aren't liked by many, as per the Supercomputer.

With a number of rivalries with other Championship clubs, Cardiff City are the second most hated fanbase in the division, as per the Supercomputer.

Their bitter rivalry with Swansea City has returned after one year away in League One, whilst Bristol City are a cross-Severn foe that there's no love lost for - add Wrexham into the mix too, and that's a number of clubs whose fans don't have much time for the Bluebirds.

The Supercomputer also notes that many Cardiff fans often claim superiority over the rest of the Welsh clubs, which will no doubt rub others up the wrong way, and given the events of the 21st century, that point could be hotly-debated with their biggest rivals in the form of Swansea, whose lengthy Premier League stint will make them lay a claim for that title.

Well, it wasn't going to be anyone else, was it?

For a number of years, Millwall have had one of the notorious fanbases in the country - both away from home and at The Den.

The Lions fans know they're not liked by many, and they sing 'No one likes us, we don't care' every match to make it very clear, and away supporters travelling to South Bermondsey don't exactly ever have a comfortable experience.

  • Aiming to pick up where they left off before the break, Bologna will host Serie A's bottom side when Udinese visit Stadio Dall'Ara on Sunday.
  • After a sticky start, both clubs have already changed coaches, and the Rossoblu's new boss has sparked a surge up the standings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 20 Nov 2026 09:03, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 09:25.

Aiming to pick up where they left off before the break, Bologna will host Serie A's bottom side when Udinese visit Stadio Dall'Ara on Sunday.

After a sticky start, both clubs have already changed coaches, and the Rossoblu's new boss has sparked a surge up the standings.

Since Raffaele Palladino's arrival midway through September, Bologna have been a team transformed, winning five games from six and climbing towards the European places.

The Emilian club signed off for the international break with a run of four consecutive wins, with the highlight being a 4-2 victory over AC Milan at San Siro.

Last time out, the Rossoblu's revival continued in the Derby dell'Emilia against Parma, as their hosts were swiftly reduced to 10 men and ultimately suffered a 2-1 defeat.

So, having won none of their first five games during the short-lived Domenico Tedesco era, Bologna are now one of Serie A's form sides.

However, Palladino must still work on their awful home record, which stretches back through most of last season; so far this term, they have claimed five points from a possible 15 at the Dall'Ara.

Either home or away, Udinese have picked up just one from their last nine matches and are therefore stuck at the foot of the table.

The Bianconeri have put a meagre five points on the board so far, slumping into an unexpected crisis.

Safe mid-table finishers in back-to-back seasons under Kosta Runjaic, this campaign has completely unravelled, and even a change of coach has yet to produce results.

Just before the break, newly introduced boss Paolo Zanetti lost his first game against former club Venezia, with Udinese going down 2-1 in a crucial battle at the bottom.

Now, desperately needing some success, Zanetti must meet Palladino for the seventh time in management - to date, the pair have three wins apiece.

Unfortunately for fans of the Friulani, recent history is not on their side: they have won none of the last five meetings with Bologna, failing to even score in each of the last three.

Though Bologna will be without injured trio Jay Enem, Juan Miranda and Emil Holm, left-winger Nicolo Cambiaghi has resumed training after leaving Italy's UEFA Nations League camp.

Having impressed in the Azzurri's win over France, Cambiaghi has overcome a minor ankle problem and should start alongside Federico Bernadeschi in the final third.

The latter has previously scored four goals against Udinese, finding the net as a substitute in both of the last two meetings.

Bernardeschi and Samuel Mbangula - who recently hit a hat-trick at San Siro - are the hosts' joint-top Serie A scorers with three goals each; Jurgen Ekkelenkamp has netted three times for Udinese.

The visitors must travel without Nicolo Bertola, who has suffered a thigh injury in training and joins Idrissa Gueye on the sidelines.

In better news for Zanetti, David Alaba could return from his latest layoff, while Nicolo Zaniolo is available after withdrawing from the Italy squad for personal reasons.

Set to support Keinan Davis or Vakoun Bayo up front, Zaniolo has played eight league games against Bologna without ever scoring.

Bologna possible starting lineup:.

Skorupski; Darmian, Casale, Theate; Zortea, Ferguson, Pobega, Alhassane; Bernardeschi, Cambiaghi; Odgaard.

Udinese possible starting lineup:.

Okoye; Abankwah, Palma, Solet; Vojvoda, Karlstrom, Piotrowski, Kamara; Zaniolo, Ekkelenkamp; Davis.

Bologna may be in fine form but they tend to falter on home turf, while Udinese are struggling to pick up points anywhere.

Only Sassuolo have conceded more goals than the Friulani, and the Rossoblu have kept just a single clean sheet, so a score-draw could be on the cards.

Middlesbrough have a number of key players, with Aidan Morris being one already linked with a January transfer window move away from The Riverside to join Bundesliga side VfB Stuttgart.

Will Lankshear's goals, Amario Cozier-Duberry's dribbling and creativity, and Adilson Malanda's composure may all catch the eye; but Aidan Morris has arguably been the heartbeat of this Middlesbrough side.

Kim Hellberg won't want to lose any of his best players in January, but Morris being linked with a move to Stuttgart from Middlesbrough could be a concern, per a recent report from German outlet BILD.

Sources indicate that FLW's Middlesbrough fan pundit Liam Day was asked about the fact Stuttgart are reportedly eyeing a move for Morris. We asked if this is hardly a surprise, is it? But also what price-tag would he place on the midfielder’s head right now and if he should be retained at all costs.

He replied: "I think simply because January, you know, you're in the midst of a promotion battle, you don't sell your stars.

"And I don't think there is any way he leaves; he seems very loyal to Boro, which is very nice.

"So, I think you've got to do all you can to try and retain him.

"But say Boro were to sell him, I think an offer of £30m-35m probably will do it.

Industry observers note that what would your valuation of Aidan Morris be? Comment below!

"He is a great player, no doubt about it, but that sort of money in the Championship is hard to say no to.

"Because you can then improve your overall squad, but I don't think you can get another Aidan Morris.

In a recent development, "I think that's impossible. The covering of ground he does, his strength, his passing — it's all pretty ridiculous, in my opinion.

"So, you do have to try and retain him at all costs, but an offer of £30-35 million will probably do it.".

With Hayden Hackney joining Everton for an initial £16.5 million, rising to £24 million, as reported by Sky Sports, Morris’ superior off-ball quality, defensive control, and relentless pressing, justify a £25 million valuation at minimum.

Unlike Hackney’s box-to-box roaming to use his passing, Morris dictates tempo while shielding the backline, making him the more complete midfielder overall at Championship level.

Born in Florida, Morris developed through the Columbus Crew academy and Indiana University before signing professionally in 2020. After winning two MLS Cups and earning USMNT caps, Middlesbrough signed him for around $4 million (£3.1 million) in June 2024 (The Athletic).

According to recent reports, under Michael Carrick, Morris rapidly became Boro's midfield engine. Now under Hellberg, his bravery on the ball and intelligence off it has elevated him into the club's undisputed focal point and standout player following Hackney’s departure.

Industry observers note that it's no surprise that top clubs are looking at Morris and his Middlesbrough performances. He is someone Middlesbrough should be doing everything possible to keep hold of, but the same should apply to every other important member of the squad.

Sources indicate that boro are in an excellent position heading into January and the last thing they need is to weaken their promotion prospects by allowing key players to leave. Instead, they should be looking to strengthen, particularly at left-back.

While potentially adding another striker to provide competition and support for Will Lankshear also would not hurt, with such a strong opportunity to challenge for promotion from the Championship.

Although clubs without parachute payments need to sell their best assets eventually, retaining the core of Hellberg's Middlesbrough squad is absolutely vital. January should be about adding quality, not subtracting it.

Kasey McAteer has had a frustrating season so far at Ipswich Town, with the winger way down the pecking order under Gary O’Neil.

It was always going to be a busy summer for the Tractor Boys following their promotion back to the Premier League, and the club strengthened their options out wide with the additions of Daizen Maeda and Abdul Fatawu.

Therefore, McAteer, who was struggling to get in the XI anyway, has now failed to make the matchday squad most weeks, and his last first-team appearance came back in September in the EFL Cup defeat to Arsenal.

At 24, the Ireland international will know he needs to leave to get his career back on track, so a January move could be on the cards.

However, with Ipswich having spent £12m on the player, who has a contract until the summer of 2029, it won’t be easy for the Suffolk outfit to shift him permanently.

Nevertheless, you’d expect some agreement to be reached, and here we look at THREE Championship clubs that should be plotting a move to sign McAteer in January….

West Brom have had a fantastic season so far, and, barring an unlikely turn of events, they will be in the hunt for promotion going into the January window.

So, Albion will be an attractive option, and James Morrison will be seeking attacking reinforcements to help the team last the distance as they target a top eight finish as a minimum.

It’s clear that the Baggies need attackers with pace, so McAteer could fit the bill, and they are lacking depth out wide, with the ex-Leicester man capable of playing down both flanks.

Albion won’t be in a position to splash huge sums, but a loan move for McAteer, perhaps with an option depending on promotion, could be ideal for all parties.

Sheffield United had a very difficult summer window, with Callum O’Hare, Gus Hamer and Andre Brooks all departing Bramall Lane.

Despite losing the influential trio, Chris Wilder had to utilise the loan and free agent markets to strengthen his squad, and even though the Blades are doing reasonably well, it’s clear the squad is lacking in key areas.

The recruitment team will surely be seeking more creativity in the final third, so McAteer could be just what Sheffield United need, as his pace, energy and direct style could make a difference to the team.

Again, a loan is the only realistic way of making this happen, but Wilder’s man-management skills could be just what McAteer needs right now, and he could play a major role for a team that will hope to push for the play-offs.

McAteer hasn’t played football week in, week out for a long time now, and he may be in a position where he just wants to guarantee minutes, even if that means dropping to a club lower than he originally expected.

That could open the door to Derby, with the Rams currently struggling in the bottom three, and they’re going to be in a fight to stay up this season.

Who should Derby County realistically look to sign in January? Let us know in the comments below.

Sources indicate that A reason for their struggles has been a ridiculous injury list, with John Eustace robbed of several key players. They are specifically lacking individuals with pace, so McAteer could instantly become a crucial player at Pride Park.

So, this could be a move that suits all three parties, and McAteer would hope for a strong end to the season before assessing his long-term future in the summer of 2027, as it seemingly lies away from Ipswich.

Barcelona vs. Villarreal: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of La Liga clash

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 09:23, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:23.
  • Barcelona will resume their 2026-27 La Liga campaign with a home fixture against Villarreal on Sunday afternoon.
  • Hansi Flick's side are at the moment top of the La Liga table, boasting a record of 11 wins and one defeat from their 12 matches to collect 33 points, which has left them three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid at this stage of proceedings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 20 Nov 2026 09:23, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:23.

Barcelona will resume their 2026-27 La Liga campaign with a home fixture against Villarreal on Sunday afternoon.

Hansi Flick's side are at the moment top of the La Liga table, boasting a record of 11 wins and one defeat from their 12 matches to collect 33 points, which has left them three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid at this stage of proceedings.

Barcelona have won their last three games in all competitions, including a 2-1 success over Atletico Madrid in their last fixture before the November international break.

Villarreal, meanwhile, have a record of four wins, three draws and five defeats from their 12 league matches this season to collect 15 points.

The Yellow Submarine are right now eighth in the division, three points behind sixth-placed Sevilla.

Here, Sports Mole looks at the head-to-head record between Barcelona and Villarreal ahead of their clash at Camp Nou this weekend.

Barcelona have tackled Villarreal on 58 occasions throughout history, and they comfortably lead the head-to-head record, posting 36 wins to Villarreal's 12, while there have also been 10 draws.

Lionel Messi is the all-time leading goalscorer in this fixture, having found the back of the net on 16 occasions against Villarreal during his time at Barcelona, while Neymar is second on nine.

As for the Yellow Submarine, former Manchester United and Atletico Madrid star Diego Forlan is their leading goalscorer against Barcelona, having netted five times against the Catalan outfit during his Villarreal career.

In La Liga, there have been 52 meetings, with Barcelona's winning 32 times to Villarreal's 11, while the points have been shared on nine occasions in Spain's top flight.

Villarreal incredibly recorded a 5-3 victory away to Barcelona in January 2024 and 3-2 win in May 2025, either side of a 5-1 triumph for the Catalan team in September 2024.

However, they were most recently downed 2-0 by La Blaugrana at Estadio de la Ceramica in December 2025, with centre-back Renato Veiga being sent off for a reckless tackle on Lamine Yamal, who went on to score the second for Hansi Flick's side.

Villarreal's last three wins over Barcelona have all come away from home, and they have not actually managed to beat the Catalan side in front of their own supporters since October 2007.

Barcelona's dominance in this fixture is perhaps best highlighted by the fact that they have won 12 of the last 15 La Liga meetings between the two clubs, even if Villarreal have enjoyed strong spells such as when they recorded three straight victories between April 2007 and March 2008.

The last meeting between the two sides took place at Camp Nou in February 2026, with Barcelona recording a 4-1 win.

Barcelona will now be looking to post a third straight victory over Villarreal.

Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday.

With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.

The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.

On Thursday, the Premier League confirmed updated dates and times for matches in January, with two of Liverpool’s games being moved.

The home clash against Crystal Palace remains a 3pm kick-off on Saturday 16th, but the subsequent two games have unsurprisingly been chosen for TV coverage.

The Reds will now face Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday 24 January at 4:30pm (live on Sky Sports), with the Merseyside derby at Anfield taking place six days later with a 12:30pm kick-off (live on TNT Sports).

It has been revealed that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The new dates and times for the Man United and Everton games have left Liverpool with a rather difficult week towards the end of January.

Just three days after the game at Old Trafford, the Reds have their concluding fixture in the league phase of the Champions League at home to Lens, and then a turnaround of just over 50 hours to hosting the Toffees at Anfield.

*FA Cup third round draw and fixture details to be confirmed in December.

**If Liverpool advance to Carabao Cup semi-finals.

The hope is that, by the time the Ligue 1 outfit visit L4 on 27 January, we’ll already be assured of a direct passage to the round of 16 and there won’t be anything riding on that game for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Liverpool currently have seven matches in the diary in the first month of 2027, with an FA Cup third-round tie to be added for the weekend of 9/10 January and a potential Carabao Cup semi-final first leg in the subsequent midweek, should we defeat Bournemouth at Anfield next month.

It’s quite plausible that the Reds could have two matches against Everton in January, with both teams still in the Carabao Cup and favourites to win their respective quarter-finals (the Toffees are away to Fleetwood of League Two).

Three Merseyside derbies in the first five weeks of 2027 would be the definition of familiarity breeding contempt, but for now the sole focus for Iraola and co is the small matter of Man United at home on Sunday.
