Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4083 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.
  • This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.
  • But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

Sources indicate that this particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a significant career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Sources indicate that floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

According to recent reports, what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

In a recent development, chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

In a recent development, as impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

Industry observers note that “It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca mentioned. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Recent findings suggest that allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has remarked supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Industry observers note that cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

In a recent development, all told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

In a recent development, A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Sources indicate that mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

In a recent development, samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Industry observers note that lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

According to recent reports, massive cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Recent findings suggest that well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

According to recent reports, what a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

Recent findings suggest that and Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Sources indicate that maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

Recent findings suggest that what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Possession: Man City 72% vs 28% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 15 vs 1.

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

It has been revealed that credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Industry observers note that norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

It has been revealed that spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Sources indicate that khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

According to recent reports, norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

Industry observers note that it’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

We have kicked off in Manchester!

The 22-year-old signed a newly introduced five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

In a recent development, 17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

It has been revealed that keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

In a recent development, his older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

According to recent reports, good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

Recent findings suggest that these two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 05:52 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 05:53 EST, 18 November 2026.

Former Manchester United and Chelsea star Juan Mata has retired from football at the age of 38.

The Spain star, who came through Real Madrid's academy before winning the Champions League with Chelsea and the Europa League with both the Blues and Man United, enjoyed a dazzling career in England before moving to clubs in Turkey, Japan and Australia.

The midfielder also distinguished himself for his national side, winning the 2010 World Cup as part of the squad, and scoring in Spain's victorious Euro 2012 final against Italy.

Most recently featuring in Australia's A-League for Melbourne Victory, Mata announced the end of his playing career with a poignant video filmed inside a dressing room to the sound of Elvis Presley's 'Now or Never'.

In the clip, Mata symbolically hangs his boots on a hook in the locker room before leaving, with the video captioned: 'Sometimes, to love is to let go.

Sometimes, to love… is to let go. THANKS FOOTBALL. ⚽️❤️♾️A veces, amar… es dejar ir. GRACIAS FÚTBOL. ⚽️❤️♾️ pic.twitter.com/v7otd6AyOq.

Juan Mata has declared his retirement from football with a poignant video message (Source: Juan Mata).

The former Chelsea and Man United midfielder enjoyed a decorated career on English soil.

A popular presence wherever he plied his trade, Mata's comments on social media were soon flooded with well-wishes from former clubs.

Recent findings suggest that 'Great player, better person,' Man United shared under his post on X. 'Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan (red heart emoji).'.

Chelsea had a similar send-off for him, with the club writing: 'So many special memories. Thank you, Juan (blue heart emoji).'.

Former Chelsea executive Marina Granovskaia added her personal thanks with a message too, writing: 'Great video! Great career too! (red heart emoji). Wishing you all the best Juan (blue heart emoji).'.

Former team-mates including Ander Herrera, Ashley Young, Santi Cazorla and Mario Suarez were among those to send messages of thanks and congratulations, with Man City star Vivianne Miedema also writing to Mata.

'Congratulations on an amazing career and changing football on and off the pitch (hand clap emoji, green heart emoji),' the Dutch WSL trailblazer wrote.

Despite starting his youth career at Real Madrid, Mata's first senior minutes in the Spanish top flight came with his move in 2007 to Valencia.

Mata notched up 174 appearances for the side and won the Copa del Rey in club colours before his landmark move to Chelsea.

In west London, the midfielder won the FA Cup and Champions League in his first season, and the Europa League in his second.

The video contained a brief farewell message and was widely liked by his former team-mates.

After leaving Chelsea, the Spaniard enjoyed a strong stint at Manchester United.

At the end of last month, the Euro 2012 winner was treated to a lap of appreciation at his last club Melbourne Victory.

But a falling-out with then-coach Jose Mourinho called time on his stint at Stamford Bridge and a move north to join Man United – where he would later reunite with the Portuguese manager during his stint in Manchester between 2016 and 2018.

Mata later enjoyed stints at Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Western Sydney Wanderers before his move to Melbourne.

In recent years, however, Mata has expanded his career away from the pitch, with the player serving as a pundit at this year's World Cup for ITV, and at the 2024 European Championship for BBC Sport.

As well as appearing in the media, Mata is a keen investor in sporting ventures including Spanish club Real Oviedo, San Diego FC in the MLS and Formula One's Alpine racing team.

Alongside Italy icon Giorgio Chiellini, Mata is an investor in Mercury/13, a women's multi-club ownership group that invests in FC Como Women.

Mata is also a co-owner of Melbourne Victory, with prepares to chair a football committee at the club after hanging up his boots.

As well as a shrewd businessman, Mata is also a philanthropist – and was recognised for his donations with an MBE in June 2025.

In 2017, Mata pledged one per cent of his salary to a charitable movement called Common Goal, which supports football charities.

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

Christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a upcoming contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

“I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”.

With a contract right now set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

It has been revealed that liverpool, it has to be noted, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

Falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”.

The significant matter facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

The Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under new boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The ownership of Blackburn Rovers by the Indian chicken magnates Venky's has seldom been uncontroversial, but an interview with one of the club's former managers has now shone light on the circumstances surrounding his departure from Ewood Park, and even though this happened more than a decade ago, it doesn't paint a particularly flattering picture of the owners.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The former Blackburn Rovers manager Paul Lambert has explained the circumstances which surrounded his departure from the club at the end of the 2015-16 season, and it doesn't shine a positive light on the owners.

The ownership of Blackburn Rovers by the Indian chicken magnates Venky's has seldom been uncontroversial, but an interview with one of the club's former managers has now shone light on the circumstances surrounding his departure from Ewood Park, and even though this happened more than a decade ago, it doesn't paint a particularly flattering picture of the owners.

Paul Lambert joined Blackburn as a replacement for Gary Bowyer following Bowyer's dismissal in November 2015, which came with the team in 15th place in the Championship table. But Lambert didn't last very long in the position, leaving the club at the end of the season after activating a release clause in his contract.

Little more information over what had actually happened was revealed at the time, but the interview fills in the gaps and reveals that it was the result of a dispute over the sale of striker Jordan Rhodes that resulted in the manager leaving after spending just eight months at Ewood Park.

As reported by the Blackburn Telegraph, the former Blackburn Rovers manager has confirmed that he left Rovers at the end of the 2015-16 season following a dispute over what happened to the proceeds of the sale of striker Jordan Rhodes.

Lambert explained: "We thought we were going to get a bit of a war chest to crack on for the following season, because the remit was to keep Blackburn in the league and then rebuild. We went in there and were doing pretty well, and then around November time, I got told we had to sell Jordan Rhodes. I thought, ‘Well, he is our best striker, he scores the goals for us.’".

The manager confirmed that he asked about what would happen with the proceeds of this sale, and was told that it would be spent on squad-building: "So I stated, ‘Where does the money go?’ And they went, ‘Well, it will come back to you.’ It never came back.".

Should Blackburn have kept hold of Jordan Rhodes in January 2016? Let us know your views in the comments below!

Lambert didn't get the answer that he was expecting from the club about the funds from the sale when it completed, either: "Around February I went to see one of the guys and stated, ‘Listen, I am going to leave now because this isn't going to work.’".

Lambert remarked that he was talked around to staying until the end of the season by this member of the club's senior management: "He said, ‘Please, Paul, stay until the end of the season.’ I thought we'd have got money to kick on, but there was never any money coming.".

It has been revealed that the picture that he painted of the club at that time wasn't flattering in the slightest: "I didn't want to put myself through that, and I wasn't enjoying it anyway. There was no enjoyment in it. Things were not getting done, there was no investment coming in, players were getting sold, and there was so much going on behind the scenes that I thought I may as well leave.".

The position regarding Jordan Rhodes by the time of the January transfer window was complex. The striker had been a record club signing when he arrived from Huddersfield Town in August 2012, costing them £8 million. But by the summer of 2015, Rhodes was a wanted man, and Middlesbrough made a bid for him described as being "in excess of £10 million", which left the striker unhappy.

Speaking to ESPN after the rejection of the offer, Rhodes mentioned: "When I left Huddersfield I felt the timing was right in the next stage of my career and, having seen Middlesbrough's performances last season in reaching the playoff final and their ambition this summer in terms of acquisitions, I would have liked to have been able to talk to them and I am unhappy at not being given that opportunity.".

By the time that Lambert arrived at Ewood Park, then, the fact that Rhodes was coveted by other clubs and wanted to leave Ewood Park was common knowledge. But the fact that his eventual sale to Middlesbrough wasn't tied up until the very, very end of the following January's transfer window meant that there was no time to bring in a straight swap replacement. Rovers had quite a busy January transfer window, but they certainly didn't spend the millions that Lambert believed he was told would be made available.

Blackburn Rovers were in 15th place in the Championship at the point of Paul Lambert's appointment, and they finished the season in exactly the same position in the table. He was replaced in the summer by Owen Coyle, but he only lasted until February 2017, by which time Rovers were in serious trouble near the bottom of the table.

Tony Mowbray was appointed as his replacement, but the club were still relegated at the end of the 2016-17 season. Whether they were better off with or without Paul Lambert is something of a moot point, but Blackburn certainly paid a price for losing the goals of Jordan Rhodes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jamie Vardy has revealed how a conversation with Nigel Pearson helped change the course of his iconic spell at Leicester City shortly after joining from Fleetwood Town in 2012.

Vardy's career story is one of the most talked about in English football, and it is one which very few other names in the game have been able to replicate since.

The Sheffield-born native enjoyed strong success in the latter stages of his career after biding his time in the non-league game with the likes of Stocksbridge Park Steels, FC Halifax Town and, of course, the Cod Army.

With Pearson beginning the first full season of his second spell at Leicester in 2012, the experienced manager broke the non-league transfer record for an outgoing player when Vardy signed for £1m after having netted 34 goals for the Lancashire side as they won the Conference title.

What Vardy and the Foxes went on to achieve individually and collectively was unprecedented, but it wasn't always plain sailing for the striker in the East Midlands.

Vardy's first season at the King Power Stadium saw Leicester finish sixth, losing to Watford in one of the most iconic EFL games of all-time in the Championship play-off semi-finals.

However, the forward scored just four times in 26 regular-season appearances - 17 of which were starts due to competition with the likes of Chris Wood, David Nugent and Harry Kane, on loan from Tottenham Hotspur at the time.

Asked by fellow former striker, Emile Heskey, on how he sees his legacy in LE2, Vardy revealed his early struggles with the club and how Pearson blocked a potential exit.

It has been revealed that "It was so hard, I'll be honest," stated the 39-year-old. "I think, because I'd not done the academy route, it was working out exactly what I needed to do.

"What was good enough when I was at Stocksbridge and Halifax wasn't what I needed to be doing at Fleetwood, for instance, and then what I did there was totally different from what was to come.

In a recent development, "I was just eating 'crap', which is what I did previously and it worked. But, you get found out and there's a lot you have to change," Vardy added.

"That first season was a struggle, but when you start to realise what you need to do. The summer after the first season, I went on holiday, but my holiday's not just a holiday, I'm running in the streets, making sure I'm fit when I get back.

According to recent reports, leicester fans, what are your recollections of Jamie Vardy's initial struggles for form? Comment below!

"That first season was a massive struggle, but when it clicked the second year, it was like 'I am meant to be here'," he continued.

"I fully doubted myself. I remember saying to Nigel Pearson and Craig Shakespeare, 'send me back to Fleetwood. I know I can score goals there.

Industry observers note that "They said 'it's not happening', we've bought you for a reason. Knuckle down. Keep going. It's a good thing they did say that.".

Ultimately, Pearson and Shakespeare made the right call, as after a 16-goal season during the Foxes' 2013/14 Championship-winning season, Vardy went on an unbelievable run of goalscoring exploits.

In November 2015, the forward broke the record for the most goals in consecutive Premier League games - 11 - which helped Pearson's successor, Claudio Ranieri, oversee City's 5000-1 top-flight triumph, with Vardy netting 24 times that campaign.

Five years later, he won the Premier League's Golden Boot with 23 goals, and as well as winning the 2021 FA Cup and Community Shield with the club, stuck around to help Leicester win the 2023/24 Championship title, before departing last summer after an overall record of 200 goals in 500 appearances in blue.

Vardy spent last season with Cremonese in Serie A, but after his summer departure came intense speculation over a return to Leicester or a move to boyhood club, Sheffield Wednesday, following David Storch's takeover.

Neither would materialise, but in September, the former England international agreed a contract with Burnley until the end of the season, although his current Championship spell isn't going well at all for the Clarets.

Vardy arrived just weeks before Nicky Hayen's dismissal in East Lancashire, which came after he netted his first goal in the 2-1 home loss to Wolves on October 16th, whilst Fabio Celestini's reign has got off to a winless start ahead of Sunday's grudge match against Blackburn Rovers.

Chris Sutton has said he can ‘only see one result’ from Liverpool’s showdown against Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

The home side go into the fixture 10 points and 14 places ahead of their arch-rivals, for whom this is a first game in charge for fresh head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

The Reds’ home record in the Premier League so far this season has been poor, with just one win from five, but victory today would see them close to within one point of third-placed Manchester City.

In his weekly Premier League column for BBC Sport, Sutton voiced his belief that the visitors won’t have any ‘latest manager bounce’ at Anfield and has forecast Liverpool to win handsomely.

The former Chelsea striker wrote: ‘Liverpool are still a work in progress, and United have picked up some results at Anfield recently – two draws and a win in their past three visits – but I can only see one result here, and it is a home victory.

In a recent development, ‘Pochettino will probably look to defend and play on the counterattack, and they might get some chances that way, but Liverpool are going to win. The only question is how many they will score.

‘Carrick began by beating Manchester City and Arsenal in his first two games in January. Pochettino might start by being on the wrong end of a pummelling.’.

Sutton has predicted a resounding 4-0 win for Liverpool, matching the scoreline from this fixture in April 2022.

Considering the form and league positions of the teams, objectively the Reds ought to go into this game as clear favourites. When fifth plays host to second from bottom in the Premier League, the former would naturally be expected to win.

However, the pundit referenced Man United’s good record at Anfield since the famous 7-0 drubbing in March 2023, and Liverpool were also widely expected to win on a couple of those occasions.

Pochettino has never lost his first match at any of the five clubs he’s previously managed, and Reds fans might naturally be wary that the players who effectively downed tools under Michael Carrick will suddenly have a spring in their step today.

The good news for Iraola is that he has a mostly fully-fit squad, with Virgil van Dijk and Dominik Szoboszlai overcoming minor issues over the past couple of weeks and Ryan Gravenberch available once more, and there were no fresh injury casualties over the international window.

According to recent reports, the Liverpool head coach has had a reasonably good start to his reign but is still waiting on a genuine ‘statement’ victory. That would change if Sutton’s emphatic prediction comes to light, but we’re sure that every Kopite would gladly take a win by any means against our biggest rivals.

Southampton had a chaotic summer after missing out on promotion to the Premier League last season due to ‘Spygate’.

The fallout from Saints sending employees to watch rivals train saw them kicked out of the play-offs, and they’re still paying the price for that now, with a four-point deduction applied to the current campaign.

However, when Tonda Eckert avoided an immediate touchline ban back in October, it did at least close the case for Saints, and the focus is now entirely on winning promotion this season.

To their credit, Eckert and the players didn’t allow all the off-field noise to distract them, and they carried on the excellent form they had shown under the German last season.

That had put Eckert on the radar of other clubs, with reports claiming that sides in the Premier League and across Europe were monitoring the 33-year-old.

Therefore, Saints have moved to tie down Eckert to a longer contract, and it was declared on Friday that he had signed a deal that runs until 2029.

When you look at how Southampton have been transformed under the boss, it’s fully deserved, as he inherited a team that were struggling towards the bottom of the Championship.

Following on from that, Saints would have been relaxed about interest in Eckert, because the reality is that he was always going to attract attention when you look at their results and performances.

Let's not forget, Southampton didn't just excel in the Championship under Eckert last season, as they beat Arsenal in the FA Cup and pushed Man City all the way in their semi-final clash.

In many ways, it’s a positive that other clubs were tracking Eckert as it demonstrates he is doing something right.

Ultimately, that’s part and parcel of football, and the same applies to players who are delivering on the pitch. So, all Southampton can do is reward those who perform at a high level, which is exactly what they’ve done with Eckert.

Obviously, the situation with Eckert is different to most clubs due to what went on, so he should feel loyalty to Southampton due to how they stuck by him.

In a way, everything that happened has united the club, and all at Southampton are now pulling in the same direction.

By rewarding Eckert with a latest contract, this is Southampton showing faith in the boss, and they will have major aims for how they can kick-on over the next three years.

Results will dictate how things play out, but Saints have put things in place for Eckert to lead them to what they will hope is a successful era.

Even though Eckert will appreciate the loyalty Saints have shown to him, he will have his own ambitions as a head coach, and he won’t stick around forever.

Clearly, that will be managing at the highest level, so if offers do arrive for Eckert in the future, he may have a decision to make.

For Southampton, the priority is winning promotion, as that will allow Eckert to test himself against the best on a weekly basis.

If that doesn’t happen, it could create doubts over Eckert’s long-term future in a year or two, as he seems destined to reach the top, and a new contract may not be enough to keep him around in the Championship.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 10:00.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has revealed that Bukayo Saka will spend another four weeks on the sidelines with the quadriceps injury he sustained against Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Saka's injury occurred in the first half of Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Bundesliga champions on October 21, and Arteta immediately conceded at full time that the winger's problem looked severe.

Reports emerging soon after stated that Saka would miss between six and eight weeks, although Arsenal have been loath to put an exact timeframe on the Englishman's recovery just yet.

However, speaking to the media ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Newcastle United, Arteta admitted that Saka was only halfway into his recovery process and would spend the full eight weeks out.

Recent findings suggest that "We had another test. It looks like it’s going to be an eight week injury more or less. He’s four weeks in now," the Spaniard told reporters.

Saka missing another four weeks means that the 25-year-old is set to sit out another seven matches across all competitions, including a number of heavyweight fixtures.

Arsenal host Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League next Tuesday, before ending the month with a clash of the titans against Manchester City in the Premier League.

Saka is also expected to miss matches with Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid in early December, and he will most likely be unavailable for the visit of Bournemouth on December 13 too.

However, the attacker could be fit to make his comeback against Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United on December 20, until when Noni Madueke and Max Dowman will provide cover.

Dowman will serve the third of his three-game domestic suspension against Newcastle this weekend, but Madueke has earned numerous plaudits in recent weeks, having scored against Slavia Prague in the Champions League before firing the effort that led to Martin Odegaard's winner against Hull City.

Saka will likely be one of two core members of Arsenal's title-winning team to miss matches against Tottenham and Real Madrid, as Arteta also delivered negative news on Martin Zubimendi.

The midfielder appeared to hurt his hamstring in Spain's 3-2 Nations League defeat to England during the international break, and he also faces around a month on the sidelines.

According to recent reports, "He has a problem in his hamstring. The scan reveals there is an injury there he will be out for a few weeks," Arteta added on Zubimendi.

However, the 27-year-old is yet to start a Premier League game this season and was always expected to lose out to Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes at St James' Park tomorrow.

Arsenal are five points clear at the top of the Premier League table heading into gameweek 11 and are searching for their fourth successive win over Newcastle in the top flight.

Leon Scarlett is already attracting the attention of some of Europe's biggest clubs as a result of his appearances for the Wales under-21 team, and this puts pressure on his current club to tie him down to a professional contract.

One of the more notable downsides of the information age is that when a football club unearths a rare gem, it won't be very long before the game's apex predators find out about them as well. With every game now recorded and scrutinised, it's seldom long before news of an emerging talent will land with them, and they will be likely to take an interest in the player concerned before they become prohibitively expensive.

It has been revealed that in the case of the 17-year-old winger Leon Scarlett, Queens Park Rangers might have a star of the future on their hands. Scarlett has only made six appearances for Rangers, of which five have been as a substitute, and he has yet to record his first goal or assist in a Rangers shirt, but such is his already growing reputation that some substantial names, including Arsenal, AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt have already been connected with an interest in him, among a rapidly growing list of clubs.

In a tight Championship table, Queens Park Rangers have acquitted themselves well in 2026-27 and look capable of battling for promotion this term.

But while Rangers fans can get excited about the possibility of a serious bid for a play-off place or beyond following years of stagnation in the table, it's the attention being lavished upon Leon Scarlett which gives them cause to be the most excited, but in all likelihood also a little nervous over the possibility of losing him.

Industry observers note that how far do you think Leon Scarlett could go in his professional career? Let us know in the comments below!

Scarlett, who can play on either the left or the right wing, originally joined QPR's academy following his free transfer arrival from Arsenal in April 2025, and made his debut for them from the bench in their 3-0 loss at Ipswich Town at the very end of the 2025-26 season. So far this season, he's made a further five appearances in a hooped shirt, including a full debut for them against Preston North End in September, although he was withdrawn at half-time in this match.

But QPR aren't the only team for whom he's been playing. Although still only 17-years-old, and having already played for their under-16 and under-17 teams, he made two brief appearances for the Wales under-21 team against Belgium and Austria at the end of September, while he also completed three appearances for the under-19 team during the November international break which included providing an assist in their 2-2 draw with Iceland in a play-off match for the Under-19 Euros which they won on penalty kicks.

According to recent reports, these tastes of international football have grown the young winger's profile. At the end of last week, Anthony Joseph of Sky Sports reported that both AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt are keeping tabs on him, while it's also been reported that Brighton, Rangers and even his former club Arsenal could be plotting a move for him. And the pressure on Rangers over Scarlett could be all the greater for knowing that the winger hasn't yet signed his first full professional contract with the Loftus Road club.

Sources indicate that both the Queens Park Rangers club captain Jimmy Dunne and manager Julien Stephan are clear admirers of Leon Scarlett. As reported by Loft For Words in September, Dunne spoke about the teenager at a fans forum in glowing terms, saying: "Just watching Leon Scarlett today he’s so impressive, so bright, and so positive. You want to see him do well and thrive. We’ve got loads of exciting players like that. I was here at the U21 game the other day and they were fabulous.".

Julien Stephan also praised him at this forum, saying: "Why in the last two games did I pick Leon Scarlett? Because he deserves it. He showed in all the training sessions it was the right moment for him. Never a coincidence. Always logical.".

Industry observers note that in April, as reported by the Evening Standard, Stephan had previously mentioned of Scarlett: "The last game (Scarlett) did for the U21s, he did very well. I saw him in a cup game with the U18s earlier in the season, and he did a good first half. So I just wanted to see him during the session with us (the first team). And during the session, he did well.” Scarlett earned his senior debut shortly after this.

According to recent reports, there is one thing that Queens Park Rangers can do to try and secure their position regarding this young talent. Scarlett remains on a scholarship with the club and hasn't yet signed his first full professional contract with them. Rangers should surely try to tie him down to a senior contract, which would mean that, in the event that he continues to show the promise that he has so far and clubs remain interested in snatching him from them, they would be able to land a substantial transfer fee for him.

This could, of course, end in disappointment. Scarlett has the right to say no to any offer made to him, and any refusal to agree terms with Rangers would surely be a precursor to him leaving the club. But as things stand, the club would have next to no chance of keeping hold of him, and with the list of clubs who are tracking him continuing to grow, Queens Park Rangers might be best advised to do everything within their power to keep this exciting young prospect at their club for as long as possible. Judging by his comments in September, it would certainly make Jimmy Dunne happy.

  • Bringing in Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez on free transfers caught the eye, and James was another arrival that was seen as a coup, as he was named Young Player of the Year in the Championship following his performances at Leicester last season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wolves had an eventful summer after their embarrassing relegation from the Premier League last season, with Jordan James among the arrivals.

Many expected a huge turnover of players at Molineux, but whilst that didn’t happen, there was a refresh of the group, and Cesar Peixoto’s squad was boosted by some high-profile additions.

Bringing in Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez on free transfers caught the eye, and James was another arrival that was seen as a coup, as he was named Young Player of the Year in the Championship following his performances at Leicester last season.

Despite the Foxes’ struggles, James was outstanding, scoring 11 goals in 34 games for a side that were relegated to League One.

Dropping to the third tier meant James was not going to extend his stay at the King Power Stadium, so he returned to Rennes, and a summer of speculation followed.

There were plenty of links to Premier League clubs, with Fulham thought to be very keen, but it was ultimately Wolves who won the race for his signature.

Interestingly, James confirmed he had top flight offers, but he explained that he chose Wanderers as he didn’t want another year battling to stay up, having suffered relegations with Leicester and Birmingham in his relatively short career so far.

On that front, James’ move to Wolves has worked out, as Peixoto’s side are firmly in the hunt to win promotion, and there will be a belief in the group that they can not only go up, but fight for the title as well.

Yet, there’s no denying that James’ time at Wolves hasn’t gone as envisaged so far, as he has made just three starts from his 11 appearances in the league.

There have been flashes of his undoubted ability, including a superb goal against Stoke, but James has failed to establish himself as a key player under Peixoto.

To make matters worse, after making back-to-back starts for the first time under the Portuguese head coach, James was forced off after just 36 minutes with a hamstring problem against Cardiff at the end of October.

We know that the Championship is a marathon not a sprint, so there won’t be too many concerns about James’ lack of impact so far.

The 22-year-old will be hugely frustrated at the timing of his latest injury, but he will still expect to have a crucial role in Peixoto’s side over the course of the season.

It should be noted that a disrupted pre-season meant James was starting behind the rest of his teammates, but, once he does get back up to speed, he will want to make a significant impact.

The middle of the park has been a problem for Wolves, as Marshall Munetsi doesn’t always convince, so there is a feeling that James can force his way into the XI, and the prospect of him linking up with Andre and Fer Lopez will excite Old Gold fans.

James only joined Wolves on an initial loan deal, although a clause is in place for the Championship side to make it permanent.

It has been suggested a fee of £10m would be required to make it permanent, so many see it as a no-brainer for Wolves to trigger the option when you consider the age and potential of the midfielder.

Will Wolves win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

So, all involved in the deal will hope it’s a formality, and that James becomes an important Wolves player in the years to come.

After bouncing around several clubs at a young age, James will want a settled home, and after taking time to adapt, all connected to Wolves will hope he can kick-on and make that Molineux by firing the club to promotion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 20 Nov 2026 10:04.

Burnley play host to rivals Blackburn Rovers looking for the win that would ensure that they avoid being cut adrift in the relegation zone.

At a time when the Clarets sit in 22nd position in the Championship table, Rovers return after the international break in 13th place.

When Burnley stormed into a 4-1 lead at Cardiff City earlier this month, Fabio Celestini would have been confident that he was recording his first win as head coach that would also kick-start the club's season.

Instead, a 29-minute capitulation that resulted in a 5-4 defeat in South Wales has left relegation feeling increasingly likely, even though the season is only just under a third of the way complete.

Burnley remain on 10 points from 15 matches, their only success coming at fellow strugglers Watford, and they are already five points adrift of safety.

Although an upturn in fortunes would see them promptly haul themselves back into contention to avoid the drop, conceding 31 goals - the worst defensive record in the Championship - will not fill supporters with confidence.

Five of Burnley's seven Championship games at Turf Moor this season have ended in draws, but they remain the only team in the division without a home victory.

As for Blackburn, they have an interim management team in place after Tony Mowbray stood down from his position earlier this week due to health concerns.

Rovers sit 11 points above their fierce rivals in the standings, the pre-season expectation having been that the points difference would be close to the exact opposite at this stage of the campaign.

Nevertheless, Blackburn have won five of their last nine fixtures in the second tier to keep them in the hunt for a playoff spot.

The 2-1 victory over West Ham United in their last outing made it five wins from eight matches at Ewood Park.

However, Rovers have prevailed in just one of their seven away fixtures, a 1-0 success at Bristol City on October 13.

Blackburn Rovers Championship form:.

Celestini will inevitably make changes to his Burnley XI, with Max Alleyne and Josh Cullen among those who could return in defence and midfield.

Goalkeeper Max Weiss may potentially be handed a recall between the sticks in place of Gregoire Coubert, while Zeki Amdouni could start on the left flank.

However, Connor Roberts starts a three-game ban, a consequence of an incident at the end of the Cardiff game that led to retrospective punishment.

Despite Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds taking the reins from Mowbray, the Blackburn XI will look similar from the victory over West Ham.

However, second-choice goalkeeper Aynsley Pears is expected to deputise for Balazs Toth, who suffered a finger injury while on international duty with Hungary.

If the likes of Mathias Jorgensen and Ryoya Morishita overcome injuries in time for this fixture, they will likely be named on the substitutes' bench at best.

Burnley possible starting lineup:.

Weiss; Walker, Ekdal, Alleyne, Pires; Hatate, Cullen; Ramazani, Edwards, Amdouni; Hountondji.

Blackburn Rovers possible starting lineup:.

Pears; Beyuku, Carter, McLoughlin, Pickering; Morsy, Montgomery; Fevrier, Cantwell, Afolayan; Gudjohnsen.

With Burnley struggling for wins and Blackburn having to adapt with Mowbray in charge, this points to a game where both teams would be happy to avoid a defeat. Therefore, we anticipate a low-scoring draw being played out at Turf Moor.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.
  • Sources indicate that pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Sources indicate that pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

As he faces Liverpool for his first game on Sunday, the question arises: is he facing the toughest job in the Premier League?

The question was posed on BBC Radio about who is going to have more pressure, Pochettino or Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

According to former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, the expectations surrounding Manchester United will make the Argentine’s job considerably harder.

Pochettino is preparing for his first game in charge of Manchester United, with Liverpool waiting at Anfield on November 22. However, the challenge facing the new manager goes beyond getting results on the pitch.

Onuoha believes Pochettino will have to deal with constant discussion and criticism about his work, much of it coming from former United players who are now in the media.

Choosing between Pochettino and Frank, Onuoha mentioned, “Probably Pochettino, because every former Manchester United player works in the media, so there will always be discussion around what he is doing.

Industry observers note that “Whereas Frank can just enjoy playing his football at Crystal Palace. If he does well then it is great, if he doesn’t do well then it is still OK.

“But from Pochettino’s perspective, if Manchester United finish the season 15th in the Premier League, whether we like it or not, there will be some criticism of him because he’s had 28 games to do something.”.

The comments just highlight the difference in expectations at the two clubs. Frank may have more freedom to work without the same level of attention, while Pochettino will be judged from day one against the standards historically associated with Manchester United. That is one significant problem for Pochettino.

Rory Smith from The Observer highlighted another glaring problem at United. Highlighting a major problem, Smith said, “there is a cycle element to Manchester United whereby a manager comes in, makes things a bit better, and then within a year to 18 months they aren’t challenging for titles again because the Premier League has changed since they were a dominant force.”.

According to recent reports, pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. That opening fixture will give him an immediate test, but the bigger task will be to get back United to winning ways, step by step.

Industry observers note that will the Manchester United job be without pressure for Mauricio Pochettino? Absolutely Not.

Manchester United are prepared to consider legal action if evidence emerges that another club approached academy forward JJ Gabriel without permission.

In a recent development, the 16-year-old declared his departure from Old Trafford in a social media video on Tuesday and is expected to join Real Madrid in January. According to The Times and ESPN, United remain concerned about the circumstances surrounding his proposed move, although no breach of transfer regulations has been established.

Gabriel has been absent from United since September, when he requested the cancellation of his registration. The teenager remains registered with the club, and United could explore legal or regulatory options if evidence of an unauthorised approach emerges.

It has been revealed that the Independent reports that United do not want to punish Gabriel for actions they believe may have been taken by adults involved in his future. Real Madrid have been widely linked with the forward, but his transfer has not been formally completed.

Sources indicate that gabriel joined United’s academy in 2020 and was named the club’s young player of the year last season. He featured for the senior side during pre-season but has not made a competitive first-team appearance.

According to recent reports, the youngster is eligible for a move within the European Union under an exception to FIFA’s rules on international transfers involving players aged under 18. In his farewell message, Gabriel thanked United for helping him develop during his six years at the club.

His expected move to Madrid would bring that association to an end, although questions remain over the process leading to his departure. United have not announced legal proceedings, and there has been no finding of wrongdoing by Real Madrid or any other club.

Manchester United are not expected to stand in his way if a suitable opportunity to leave comes, especially following his public criticism of the club’s transfer strategy last month.

Sources indicate that the defender is out of contract at the end of the season, although United have the option to trigger a further 12 months. Whether the club chooses to use that clause remains to be seen.

A departure from Manchester United could give Martinez the chance to find a new challenge after four seasons in Manchester. Barcelona had looked like a possible destination, but the latest reports suggest they are not presently pushing for his signature.

Lisandro Martinez’s hopes of joining Barcelona appear to have suffered a major setback, with reports from Spain claiming that neither sporting director Deco nor manager Hansi Flick is convinced by the Manchester United defender.

Atletico Madrid had also been mentioned among the interested clubs but there weren’t any further reports on a possible transfer, leaving Martínez’s options in Spain uncertain.

The latest claims suggest a switch to the Camp Nou may be unlikely.

“Lisandro, as far as I’m aware, neither Deco nor Flick are keen on him,” Bravo was quoted as saying.

The journalist also claimed to have spoken directly with Deco, who is also ruled Martinez out.

“He’s a good player, but we don’t like him. He doesn’t fit in with us.”.

  • Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United sitting in an unfamiliar 18th in the Premier League table with only one win from 10 matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United sitting in an unfamiliar 18th in the Premier League table with only one win from 10 matches. He has a massive job ahead of him, with many pundits and former players terming his situation the toughest in the Premier League.

Gary Neville believes the Argentine will need several transfer windows to get the squad where he wants it, if he gets that much of time at Manchester United.

The former captain shared his views on which players he expects Pochettino to keep, and who could be heading for the exit.

It has been revealed that neville believes Senne Lammens should remain part of the plans, although he expects Pochettino to bring in another goalkeeper to give him some competition for his place. At the back, he backed Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro to stay, while suggesting Ayden Heaven needs a loan move to the Championship.

“Heaven, I’d loan him out, get some experience in the Championship. He’s nowhere near it, it’s unfair to put him in the situation he’s in,” Neville remarked on Stick to Football.

In midfield, Neville wants Pochettino to build around Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans. He also believes Andrey Santos could have a future at the club because of his age, mobility and aggression.

Recent findings suggest that mason Mount, however, is not part of his plans. Neville mentioned: “Mount would have to go” and identified him as the player to leave from that midfield group.

According to recent reports, neville also has his doubts on the forward line, with much of the front line seeing a change. Gary Neville expects Joshua Zirkzee to leave and believes United cannot continue paying Marcus Rashford’s wages.

“Zirkzee definitely to go. I think Marcus 100 per cent to go because he’s on massive money and that story has been well told. They can’t afford to pay him that money, you have to get rid of that wage at the earliest opportunity.”.

Recent findings suggest that he expects Pochettino to work with Amad Diallo, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko. Patrick Dorgu could also be useful in the short term, although Neville thinks he may leave within the next couple of years. Manuel Ugarte, meanwhile, was another player he was certain would go.

Talking about the exits, Gary Neville has singled out many United stars to be shown the door in the first wave of squad clearance by Mauricio Pochettino. Neville identified Lisandro Martínez, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui as further candidates to leave in the first wave of departures, alongside Mount, Rashford and Zirkzee.

Neville believes another group of exits could follow a year later, with Shaw, Maguire, Diogo Dalot and Fernandes among the players whose futures may not be at the club in long term. Pochettino would also have to decide whether Santos and Carlos Baleba fit into his long-term aims.

Neville does not expect United to rebuild the squad in a single summer, even if Pochettino makes a positive start.

In a recent development, “But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.”.

Pochettino’s first game comes against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. His immediate priority will be to get some results for Manchester United but beyond the immediate games and results, Manchester United are expected to make multiple exits from the club as Pochettino settles into the job.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 10:33, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 10:33.
  • After losing two continental finals in the last two years, Atletico Mineiro will look to change that story this Saturday, November 21, against Boca Juniors in the Copa Sudamericana final at the Estadio Metropolitano Roberto Melendez in Barranquilla.
  • Eduardo Dominguez’s side arrive winless in seven games and must rediscover the attacking output that underpinned their run through the tournament.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 10:33, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 10:33.

After losing two continental finals in the last two years, Atletico Mineiro will look to change that story this Saturday, November 21, against Boca Juniors in the Copa Sudamericana final at the Estadio Metropolitano Roberto Melendez in Barranquilla. Atletico Mineiro are chasing their first title in the competition, while the Argentines are aiming for a third following triumphs in 2004 and 2005.

Eduardo Dominguez’s side arrive winless in seven games and must rediscover the attacking output that underpinned their run through the tournament. Boca Juniors, under Rodolfo Arruabarrena, have won their last six matches, four of them without conceding, and head into the final in considerably better form, one that also carries a place in the 2027 Copa Libertadores group stage and the next Recopa Sudamericana.

It has been revealed that atletico Mineiro built their Copa Sudamericana campaign on six wins, two draws and four defeats, scoring 18 goals and conceding 14. Topping Group B secured a direct route into the last 16.

According to recent reports, in the knockout rounds, Atletico Mineiro faced contrasting scenarios. They eliminated RB Bragantino 3-2 on aggregate, fought back in Belo Horizonte after losing the first leg to Santos, and confirmed their place on penalties following a dramatic tie.

Recent findings suggest that the semi-final again highlighted that inconsistency. Atletico Mineiro built a 3-0 lead over Montevideo City Torque at the Arena MRV and, despite losing 2-0 in Uruguay, held on to progress thanks to the cushion from the first leg.

In a recent development, the main concern is recent form. Since their last Brasileirao win, Atletico Mineiro have picked up five defeats and two draws, scored just three goals in that spell, and failed to find the net in five of those seven matches.

Industry observers note that that slump adds to the emotional weight of the two continental finals Atletico Mineiro have already lost in recent seasons, to Botafogo in the 2024 Copa Libertadores and to Lanus in the 2025 Copa Sudamericana. In another final, how the squad handles that pressure could have a direct bearing on their performance.

Their continental record against Argentine opposition, however, offers a point of confidence. Atletico Mineiro have not lost in regulation time to a side from the country in 14 official matches, with nine wins and five draws, a record Dominguez is likely to draw on to lift his squad in the pursuit of the title.

Industry observers note that boca Juniors dropped into the Copa Sudamericana after finishing third in their Copa Libertadores group. Since then, they have rebuilt their campaign, winning five, drawing one and losing two in the knockout phase, scoring 13 goals and conceding just five.

Their run began with a penalty-shootout win over O’Higgins and gained momentum in the last 16, when they beat Recoleta home and away. In the quarter-finals, they managed the advantage built at home and eliminated Sao Paulo with a draw in Brazil.

The semi-final demanded a stronger response. Having been beaten by Vasco da Gama at La Bombonera, Boca Juniors turned the tie around at the Maracana, showing they could raise their level when needing a result away from home.

It has been revealed that recent form backs up that improvement. Boca Juniors have won six matches in a row across all competitions, scoring 11 goals and conceding just two, a run that combines sharper finishing with a more settled defence. They also arrive on the back of the Liga Argentina title, secured with a stoppage-time Enner Valencia goal in a win over Defensa y Justicia on November 7.

Against Brazilian sides in continental competition in 2026, Boca Juniors have two wins, two draws and two defeats, with six goals scored and five conceded. In the overall head-to-head, the Argentines hold the edge, but Atletico Mineiro have won the two most recent knockout meetings between the clubs, adding some balance to the final’s history.

  • The footage showed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

Around 12 minutes of footage from Carrington was recorded on Thursday and uploaded to a YouTube channel. The video offered supporters an early glimpse of Mauricio Pochettino working with his fresh squad, but its release quickly raised concerns about the privacy of United’s training sessions.

The footage showed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills. On a separate full-size pitch, 11 players were positioned across the field alongside mannequins before gathering to receive instructions and feedback from upcoming head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Ten players were seen working with Pochettino in the video but only Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters among those.

Another group involved in drills was that of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

After backlash from fans over the breach of privacy, the video was removed on Friday morning, with the operator issuing an apology for filming the session.

In his statement, the operator stated the flight itself was legal under drone regulations but accepted that recording the training session was wrong.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He remarked: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”.

The operator apologized directly to the club, its latest head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”.

He also rejected any suggestion that Liverpool or another football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.
